Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National I wanted a 5% fare increment, but transport operators are strong negotiators – Transport Minister Source : Albert Kuzor 22 November 2026 5:17pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Transport Minister Joseph Bukari Nikpe has disclosed that he initially proposed a 5% increase in public transport fares, but the negotiations with transport operators resulted in an 8% adjustment.
According to him, the proposed 5% increase contributed to a week-long negotiation with transport unions, who pushed for a higher adjustment before the final rate was agreed.
“Actually, I wanted 5%, and that delayed the one-week negotiation we were having. But you know they are also strong negotiators, so they were able to move to the 8%,” he stated on TV3's Hot Issues, Sunday, November 22.
GPRTU increased transport fares by 8%, effective Saturday, September 26, 2026.
The Deputy Public Relations Officer (PRO) of the GPRTU, Samuel Amoah, said the decision was reached after a final meeting with the Ministry of Transport on Tuesday, September 22, to discuss the proposed adjustment in fares.
According to him, the Union initially pushed for a 30% increase, arguing that failing to adjust fares would negatively affect drivers and transport operators.
“We were pushing for 30% and not coming down. But then during the meeting, the Minister also said that the President has given some directive and that hopefully we will have some more reduction on petroleum products."
The Minister explained that although there were discussions about maintaining the existing fares, the Union insisted that some adjustment was necessary to sustain operations.
